title: fix: preserve fractional image usage without rebuilding history
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fixes successful Replicate image events being quarantined when provider usage contains fractional megapixels. Writes full quantities to Float64 fields and omits fractional values from legacy UInt32 fields, preserving prices.
- Adds image-unit columns with defaults from historical integer values; updates Activity JSON/CSV, weekly classification, hourly aggregates, and Grafana queries. Uses in-place ALTER operations without copying the 422-million-row source or rebuilding downstream history.
- Validated: 34 scoped Enter/Gen tests, both typechecks, live staging ingestion/exports/hourly sums with zero quarantine, and pre-migration integer history in all three tables. Staging deployment #180 is live; image-only staging/production dry-runs reported no data copy or token changes.
- Rollout: deploy image-only Tinybird definitions before Gen/Enter producers and Grafana. Production is not deployed; retained quarantine replay is separate follow-up work. V3 canonical units and legacy-column cleanup: #15937 under #15935.
- Supersedes #15134 and #15230; credits both contributors. Addresses #15132.

gist.headline: Half a megapixel counts
gist.blurb: Fractional megapixels are still megapixels. Replicate image usage keeps its precision instead of getting sent to quarantine, with prices intact.
gist.summary: Successful Replicate image events with fractional megapixel usage are stored in Float64 image-unit fields rather than quarantined; fractional values are omitted from legacy UInt32 fields, preserving prices without copying the 422-million-row source or rebuilding downstream history.
gist.impact: Activity JSON and CSV exports, weekly usage classification, hourly totals, and Grafana queries account for fractional image units while existing integer history remains available.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy observability workbench: Polli carefully measures a half-filled pixel-art image tile on a ruler marked in megapixels, while a CRT monitor robot records the precise value. A code-plant and lime-green display connect the scene to usage data; intact stacks of old records represent history left undisturbed.
